scientific_hypothesis: Constraining thickness initialization to a bounded quasi-periodic schedule centered at ~1050 nm with [750, 1250] nm bounds, combined with a two-phase optimizer (pair-wise joint optimization followed by decoupled fine-tuning), will preserve local optical phase continuity and reduce destructive interference spikes compared to unconstrained initialization.
expected_advantages: Reduced destructive interference spikes compared to round 2
Better phase continuity across layer interfaces
known_risks: May not reach iteration_01's 0.955 score due to tighter bounds
Two-phase optimizer may converge to local minima
expected_observations: best_target_score should increase across rounds as cavity thicknesses converge to resonance conditions
tightest_margin should remain positive if both transmission bands are achievable simultaneously
valid_candidates count should remain high if 22-layer topology is physically realizable
If hypothesis fails, best_target_score will plateau below 0.7 with tightest_margin declining
stop_conditions: if best_target_score improves by less than 1e-3 against the historical best for two consecutive rounds, treat the axis as exhausted, stop and keep the current best
if valid_candidates drops below 5 for three consecutive rounds, relax the 24-layer constraint interpretation and continue with current topology
